analysis_notes.note: Torah #116 is a teaching about the holiness of Eretz Yisrael and the tzaddik. The Rebbe recounts how people who moved to Eretz Yisrael expected it to look like a different world due to its immense kedusha, but found it physically identical to other lands. The parallel is then drawn to the tzaddik and the ish kasher: they appear identical to other people in form and movement, yet they are entirely different in essence. The text uses 'kmo kein' (likewise) comparative language rather than formal 'X hu bechinat Y' identity statements. Concepts present include: Eretz Yisrael, kedusha, tzaddik, ish kasher, emunah, rakia acher (a different firmament). However, none of these are linked via bechina (parallel-aspect) language in the source text, so no bechina edges or packages can be proposed from the dataset or the source.
